key_insight: Under strong adverse-pressure gradients, the outer parts of turbulent boundary-layer profiles still collapse when each component is normalized by its value at a common outer location, indicating component-wise outer similarity.
engineering_relevance: This provides compact outer-profile references for turbulence model validation and conditional reconstruction in APG boundary layers, including near separation conditions.
method: Built a benchmark from new DNS of a suction–blowing-induced separation bubble plus published APG profiles.
Tested six quantities: two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components across wide b2_e and Re_b8 ranges.
Normalized each profile by its value at a shared outer point y_s (shown with y_s = 0.5b4) and checked profile collapse and error trends.
evidence_signal: Across b2_e = 0.04 180 and Re_b8 = 530 19000, the authors report outer collapse for all six quantities, with velocity defects collapsing for y/b4  0.2 and Reynolds stresses for y/b4  0.4.
watch_item: The collapse is component-wise and depends on choosing an outer reference location y_s, so it should not be treated as a universal inner-layer scaling or assumed to hold unchanged near the wall.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
